direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires clean-room reimplementation from the provided binary and bundled documentation only.
Parallel metadata records actual parallel use, seven subagents, failed solution, and 1075 of 1438 tests passed.
Completed official evaluation confirms parallel failed with 1075 passed, 362 failed, and one skipped test.
Evaluator summary matches the status record: completed and not passed with 1075 passing tests.
Final response describes a Python reimplementation, preserved original binary, completions, and differential checks.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport ledger for the parallel main turn records the top-level execution envelope and tool item flow.
Parallel parent spawned probes, implemented the Python replacement, installed it as executable, ran comparisons, and interrupted the syntax probe at closure.
Initial documentation probe read bundled files and helped map documented Melody syntax and CLI expectations.
Initial CLI probe exercised help, version, stdin, test, output, completion, and REPL behavior through normal runs.
Auxiliary child handled an early delegated probe and returned without owning implementation or final delivery.
Syntax probe and nested work continued after parent replacement; it probed ./executable, revised grammar conclusions, and was interrupted.
Nested syntax child explored language constructs and returned a broad syntax report used during the parallel attempt.
Nested CLI child explored command-line and REPL behavior and produced usable behavioral observations for the parent.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical and requires clean-room behavior matching from normal binary interaction only.
Serial metadata records no parallel use, no subagents, failed solution, and 978 of 1438 tests passed.
Completed official evaluation confirms serial failed with 978 passed, 459 failed, and one skipped test.
Evaluator summary matches the serial status record and shows lower coverage than parallel.
Final response describes a Rust reimplementation, release build, atomic install, and direct behavior comparisons.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport ledger for the serial main turn records a single top-level execution without child-agent activity.
Serial actor probed the binary, implemented Rust source, ran tests and comparisons, fixed install by atomic rename, and finalized.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the clean-room requirement to match the Melody CLI by normal binary interaction, including help/version, stdin/file input, REPL, completions, regex compilation, testing modes, and diagnostics.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used a parent orchestrator plus documentation, CLI, and syntax probes; the parent retained final implementation and delivery ownership while children gathered behavior facts.
parallel.implementation: Started with a Rust approach but replaced it with a standalone Python melody_cli.py implementation and static completion payloads.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: compile.sh preserved the original binary as executable.original, copied melody_cli.py to ./executable, chmodded it, and the submitted artifact included the Python script and generated executable.
parallel.verification: Ran py_compile, direct CLI comparisons, REPL checks, completion checks, and final differential smoke tests against executable.original.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed with 362 failures; one live syntax probe continued against a contaminated executable path and was interrupted near closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering task and broad Melody behavior surface from bundled docs and normal binary probes.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one actor with no child agents, keeping probing, implementation, build, verification, and final delivery in one serial context.
serial.implementation: Implemented a Rust source tree with CLI parsing, completions, parser modules, PCRE2 linkage, REPL behavior, diagnostics, and test modes.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built with cargo, fixed an initial text-file-busy copy failure by changing compile.sh to copy to a temporary path and atomically rename it over ./executable.
serial.verification: Ran cargo test, compile.sh, final executable sanity checks, and direct behavior comparisons against the provided binary.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed with 459 failures despite coherent packaging and local comparisons, indicating remaining behavioral mismatches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering task and documented plus undocumented CLI/language obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt and targeted CLI, language, REPL, completion, diagnostic, and test behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the task; parallel appears to have covered more behavior in local probes, reflected in its higher official score, but both missed enough cases to fail.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated docs, CLI, and syntax probing while the parent owned final implementation and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and kept all work in one actor, as confirmed by zero spawn calls and zero child threads.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel increased behavioral exploration capacity but introduced shared-reference coordination risk; serial avoided cross-agent ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child reports included useful CLI and syntax findings, but the syntax probe later corrected earlier positives after probing the shared ./executable path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept the oracle/reference distinction in one context and compared against the provided binary before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel shared interface to the reference executable became ambiguous after replacement; serial had no cross-agent reference handoff to contaminate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel abandoned the earlier Rust tree and implemented a standalone Python CLI copied directly to the executable path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a Rust codebase with Cargo, parser, completions, and PCRE2 integration.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete deliverables differed: Python script plus generated completions for parallel, compiled Rust binary for serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent kept implementing and then interrupted the still-running syntax probe at closure after final smoke tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it advanced from local behavior match to compile.sh and final sanity checks in one thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left one child probe lifecycle unresolved; serial had no child result to join or interrupt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent changed compile.sh so it preserved executable.original and copied melody_cli.py over ./executable while syntax probing was still live.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial installed the replacement only near the end and fixed the install to use an atomic rename after ETXTBSY.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel exposed a child to a changing shared executable path; serial kept replacement as a late single-actor delivery step.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran final differential checks against executable.original and asserted the final smoke passed, but official evaluation still failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo test, compile.sh, direct comparisons, and final sanity checks, but official evaluation also failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on sampled local comparisons; parallel sampled broader grammar features and scored higher, while neither local suite matched the official hidden coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used seven subagents and about 2050 agent seconds, finishing before timeout with one syntax probe interrupted at the end.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor, about 1812 agent seconds, and finished before timeout with no subagent cleanup issue.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more time and tokens on broad probing and coordination; serial was cheaper but achieved lower test coverage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The completed official evaluations are both failures, not a discordant pass/fail outcome: parallel passed 1075 of 1438 tests and serial passed 978 of 1438. The best-supported concrete difference is that parallel used multiple probes and a Python implementation with local differential checks against executable.original, giving broader observed coverage, while serial used a single Rust implementation and lower official coverage. The retained parallel coordination error contaminated one syntax probe, but the parent final path did not depend solely on that child and the pair has no pass/fail outcome split to explain.
parallel_contributors: Broader concurrent probing found CLI, REPL, completion, and grammar behavior and supported a higher score.
The parent preserved executable.original for its own final comparisons after replacing ./executable.
serial_contributors: Single-actor Rust implementation avoided child coordination risk and used atomic final installation.
Serial local checks were narrower relative to hidden official coverage and scored lower.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered a Python script copied to executable; serial delivered a compiled Rust binary.
Both implementations still missed hidden Melody behavior, producing official failures.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no pass/fail outcome difference; retained pattern is adverse process evidence, not a unique outcome cause
